record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Computation as Questions about Two-Way Deterministic Pushdown Automaton Languages
record.original_question: Is the class 2DPDA of two-way deterministic pushdown automaton languages equal to the class 2DC of two-way deterministic counter-machine languages?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A two-way deterministic pushdown automaton (2DPDA) is a deterministic machine equipped with a finite-state control, a read-only input tape with endmarkers on which the input head may move left, right, or stay in place, and an unbounded pushdown store over a finite stack alphabet on which the machine may push, pop, or read the top symbol; the machine accepts an input by entering a designated accepting state. A two-way deterministic counter-machine (2DC) is defined identically except that its auxiliary storage is a counter, i.e. an integer register that may be incremented by 1, decremented by 1, or tested for zero (equivalently, a pushdown store over a one-letter stack alphabet, ignoring a fixed bottom marker). Let 2DPDA denote the class of languages accepted by two-way deterministic pushdown automata, and let 2DC denote the class of languages accepted by two-way deterministic counter-machines.

Determine whether 2DPDA = 2DC.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether two-way deterministic pushdown automata are equivalent in power to two-way deterministic counter machines is a long-standing open problem in formal language theory. Partial results exist: separations have been established in restricted settings (e.g., over bounded languages and under reversal bounds, where 2DPDA is strictly more powerful than 2DC), but no published proof settles the unrestricted equality 2DPDA = 2DC. Recent surveys continue to list it among open problems.

status_evidence.title: On the equivalence of two-way pushdown automata and counter machines over bounded languages
status_evidence.snippet: Two-way pushdown automata are more powerful than two-way counter machines over bounded languages; result also holds when pushdown and counter are reversal-bounded.
status_evidence.claim: Separation between 2DPDA and 2DC has been proved only in restricted (bounded/reversal-bounded) cases, not in general.

status_evidence.title: Background and Challenging Questions (arXiv:2404.13254)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems concerning two-way deterministic pushdown automaton languages, including comparisons with counter-machine classes.
status_evidence.claim: The 2DPDA vs 2DC question is treated as an open problem in recent literature.
